references.text: The tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month in the second year. This provides the context for the timing mentioned in Numbers 10:11, which occurs a month and twenty days later.
Describes how the cloud lifted from the tabernacle as a sign for the Israelites to break camp, following the same principle observed here.
The census took place on the first day of the second month in the second year, nineteen days before the departure described in 10:11.
Provides a detailed description of how the cloud over the tabernacle directed Israel's journey—when it lifted, they broke camp.
Specifically notes that when the cloud lifted from the tent, the Israelites broke camp, and wherever the cloud stopped, they made camp.
Refers to the 'tabernacle of testimony' (mishkan ha'edut), the same expression used in Numbers 10:11.
The Israelites arrived at the Wilderness of Sinai in the third month after leaving Egypt. They are now departing from Sinai after nearly a year.
